{{Short description|Annual association football award event in France}} {{Infobox award | name = 1997 Ballon d'Or | image = Ronaldo Cannes (cropped).jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = 1997 Ballon d'Or winner, Ronaldo | date = 23 December 1997 | location = | presenter = ''[[France Football]]'' | host = | website = {{URL|ballondor.com}} | award1_type = Won by | award1_winner = {{flagicon|BRA}} [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]] (1st award) | award2_type = | award2_winner = | award3_type = | award3_winner = | award4_type = | award4_winner = | award5_type = | award5_winner = | previous = [[1996 Ballon d'Or|1996]] | main = [[Ballon d'Or]] | next = [[1998 Ballon d'Or|1998]] }} The '''1997 Ballon d'Or''', given to the best [[Association football|football]] player in Europe as judged by a panel of sports journalists from [[UEFA]] member countries, was awarded to [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]] on 23 December 1997.{{Cite web | url = https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/europa-poy97.html | title = European Footballer of the Year ("Ballon d'Or") 1997 | first = José Luis | last = Pierrend | publisher = [[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|RSSSF]] | date = 26 March 2005 | accessdate = 5 November 2013 | archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20130314042148/http://rsssf.com/miscellaneous/europa-poy97.html| archivedate= 14 March 2013 | url-status= live}} The Brazilian became the youngest winner of the award, at 21 years old.{{cite web |author=GiveMeSport |title=Who is the youngest ever Ballon d'Or winner?
